prompt.context: The federal government of a country is investigating whether to restart a rubber factory in the western part of the country. The factory was operational in the past but has not been used for 7 years. The plant was closed due to terrorism in the area, which has now come down significantly though there are still issues and skirmishes reported in the area. If rejuvenated, the plant may become a target for rebels. All the equipment is considered useable but the government still estimates spending $12M to rejuvenate the plant, which would enable it to produce up to 10M lbs of rubber per month. The demand for rubber worldwide is strong, but rubber must be transported to an export port via trains; up to 2 trains per day can be used for this.
prompt.question: Should the government go ahead with the $12M investment to restart the rubber plant? Please assess the financial viability and other key considerations.

clarifying_info.q: What are the raw materials needed?
clarifying_info.a: The plant needs gum resin. 3 lbs of resin after processing results in 1 lb of rubber.

clarifying_info.q: Where does the resin come from?
clarifying_info.a: Resin needs to be transported from the capital. Up to 4 trains per day can be used for this.

clarifying_info.q: What price can rubber be sold at? What does resin cost?
clarifying_info.a: Rubber sells at $20 per lb; gum resin costs $5 per lb.

clarifying_info.q: How many suppliers are there for resin?

clarifying_info.a: The rubber would be sold in the commodity market to the entire world.
Market demand is strong; assume that whatever the plant produces can be sold.

exhibits.title: Outgoing Train Information (Rubber)
exhibits.shows: A table showing the capacity parameters for outgoing trains carrying rubber to the export port

exhibits.title: Incoming Train Information (Resin) and Other Financial Data
exhibits.shows: A table showing the capacity parameters for incoming trains carrying gum resin, plus other plant financial information

framework: 1. Financial Analysis: Calculate ROI — map the value chain (Supplier → Plant → Customers), identify transportation constraints, determine actual production capacity, build an income statement, and compute payback period
2. Non-Financial Benefits: Employment (labor-intensive at $8MM/month payroll), economic development of the region
3. Risk Assessment & Mitigation: Terrorism risk, low margins and commodity price exposure, labor risks, supply chain risks (sole transport mode, single supplier)
4. Recommendation: Go/No-go with supporting numbers and next steps

questions.prompt: What is the monthly production capacity of the rubber plant? Perform all calculations on a monthly basis assuming 25 working days per month.
questions.guidance: Candidate must NOT simply accept 10MM lbs/month (equipment max). They must work through both the outgoing train constraint (limits rubber shipped out) and the incoming train constraint (limits resin supplied), then identify the binding bottleneck. Drawing a value chain (Supplier → Plant → Customers) is the recommended approach.

math.setup: Calculate daily and monthly capacity for outgoing rubber trains and incoming resin trains separately, then convert resin capacity to rubber using 3:1 ratio, and find the binding constraint.
steps: Outgoing (rubber): 2 trains * 8 bogies/train * 25 cases/bogie * 500 lbs/case = 200,000 lbs/day
Outgoing monthly: 200,000 * 25 = 5,000,000 lbs of rubber per month
Incoming (resin): 4 trains * 10 bogies/train * 25 barrels/bogie * 640 lbs/barrel = 640,000 lbs of resin/day
Incoming monthly: 640,000 * 25 = 16,000,000 lbs of resin per month
Resin converted to rubber: 16,000,000 / 3 = 5,333,333 lbs of rubber per month
Binding bottleneck: outgoing train capacity at 5,000,000 lbs/month
math.answer: Monthly production is capped at 5,000,000 lbs of rubber by the outgoing train capacity. The incoming resin supply can support ~5.33MM lbs, so outgoing trains are the true constraint.

questions.prompt: Build the monthly income statement for the plant and calculate the ROI on the $12M investment.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use 5MM lbs rubber produced, $20/lb selling price, 15MM lbs resin needed (5MM * 3), $5/lb resin cost, transportation cost using all 6 trains per day (4 in + 2 out), labor and fixed overhead as given. ROI = annual profit / $12M investment.

math.setup: Revenue = output * price; Material cost = resin input * resin price; Transportation = (inbound + outbound trains per day) * days * cost per trip; then subtract all costs from revenue.
steps: Material cost: 15,000,000 lbs resin * $5/lb = $75MM/month (note: resin is $5/lb not $15/lb; the casebook states material cost line as $75MM implying 15MM * $5 = $75MM)
ROI payback period: $12M investment / $12MM annual profit = 1 year
math.answer: Monthly profit = $1MM; annual profit = $12MM; payback period = 1 year. Profit margin is approximately 1% — very thin.

questions.prompt: What other areas would you explore to make a recommendation to the government?
questions.guidance: Candidate should move beyond financials to cover: (1) non-financial government benefits such as employment and regional economic development; (2) risks with concrete mitigations — low margin/commodity price exposure, labor risk, terrorism risk, and supply chain risk from sole transport mode and single supplier; (3) upside potential from relieving the transportation bottleneck.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key risks of this investment and how would you mitigate them?

categories.name: Financial / Margin Risk
ideas: Wafer-thin 1% margin; highly sensitive to resin and rubber price fluctuations
Mitigation: forward contract purchases of resin; forward contract sales of rubber

categories.name: Terrorism Risk
ideas: Plant is in an area with ongoing skirmishes and could become a rebel target
Mitigation: involve community leaders in the process; engage government or private security for the plant

categories.name: Labor Risk
ideas: Labor-intensive process ($8MM/month); shortage risk in a conflict-affected region
Mitigation: introduce automation where feasible; facilitate migration of labor from other areas

categories.name: Supply Chain Risk — Transportation
ideas: Sole dependency on trains for both inbound resin and outbound rubber
Mitigation: maintain safety stock of resin and rubber; protect rail tracks in sensitive areas; diversify into roads and waterways; invest in road infrastructure

categories.name: Supply Chain Risk — Supplier
ideas: Single identified supplier for gum resin

categories.name: Upside / Growth
ideas: Production bottlenecked by outgoing trains, not by plant capacity or resin supply
Increasing outgoing train frequency or capacity could significantly boost profits

recommendation: Go ahead with the $12M investment. The plant generates $1MM profit per month ($12MM/year), achieving full payback in 1 year.
Production will run at 5MM lbs/month, constrained by outgoing train capacity — not by equipment or resin supply — providing a clear lever to grow profits further.
risks: Margins are extremely thin at ~1%; any adverse movement in resin or rubber commodity prices could eliminate profitability
Terrorism and security risk remains active and could disrupt operations or deter labor
Single supplier and sole reliance on rail transport create significant supply chain fragility
next_steps: Assess how the plant can be staffed given the conflict-affected region
Evaluate feasibility of increasing outgoing train capacity or alternative transport modes to relieve the bottleneck and grow profits
Determine level of terrorism threat and implement community engagement and security measures
Explore forward contracts on resin and rubber to lock in the margin
